_why: The adoption procedure lived only in READ Step 3.5, and READ Step 0a HALTS on a loaded session — so the one operation you need precisely BECAUSE you are mid-session was reachable only through a mode that refuses to run there, and the `pending-handovers` scan that discovers a brief was READ Step 1. Observed 2026-09-07: an inbound brief landed mid-session and every step had to be hand-executed. Each row restores one way the new mode becomes unreachable, unsafe, or a second drifting copy of READ.

mutations.name: the-mode-vanishes-from-the-routing-table
mutations._mechanism: The section exists and nothing routes to it. A mode you can only reach by reading the file is the hand-execution this replaces.

mutations.name: the-frontmatter-still-advertises-four-modes
mutations._mechanism: The description is the surface an invocation is matched against. A mode missing from it is documentation of something that never runs — strictly worse than no mode, because the section makes it look handled.
mutations.find: Use this skill in five modes.
mutations.replace: Use this skill in four modes.

mutations.name: the-halt-exception-loses-its-reason
mutations._mechanism: An unexplained exception to a safety gate is the thing a later reader either DELETES (restoring the hand-execution this mode replaces) or COPIES to a mode with no such justification. Aimed at the REASON SENTENCE, not the bold header above it: a row against the header SURVIVED, because the paragraph beneath still carried the contrast and the test still passed. The mutation was mis-specified, not the assertion.
mutations.find:
READ's halt exists
because a resume *replaces* context — the prior session's working assumptions would silently outrank
the document just read. A takeover *adds* one owned item and replaces nothing, so that conflict cannot
arise.
mutations.replace: The halt does not apply here.

mutations.name: READ-regrows-its-own-copy-of-the-claim
mutations._mechanism: Two adoption procedures, internally consistent, drifting apart — precisely the shared-sentence divergence h_mad_adoption_check.py exists to catch, and neither reader can see it from their own copy.
mutations.find: §"TAKEOVER mode" in full — the procedure lives there, single-sourced
mutations.replace: the steps below — copied here for convenience: run `h_mad_state_write.py --claim`, single-sourced

mutations.name: takeover-stops-disclaiming-the-resume-work
mutations._mechanism: Without the never-list the mode grows into a resume — syncing, reconciling and rebuilding the todo list on a loaded session, which is exactly what READ's halt exists to prevent. The exception would then have eaten the rule.
mutations.find: - It does **not** sync with the remote, locate this branch's newest handoff, or read it.
mutations.replace: - It may sync and reconcile if that seems useful.

mutations.name: the-discovery-scan-is-dropped-from-the-mode
mutations._mechanism: Half the original gap was DISCOVERY: `pending-handovers` was READ Step 1, so mid-session you could not learn a brief had arrived. A takeover mode that cannot find one only helps when you already knew.
mutations.find: ### Step T1: Find what is addressed to this repo
mutations.replace: ### Step T1: Assume the user handed you the path

mutations.name: an-unnamed-feature-leaves-the-work-unowned
mutations._mechanism: THE live defect, 2026-09-07: the brief named no feature, the state file held 34 records, and the mode said nothing about that case — so five adopted items sat owned by nobody, which is the failure this mode exists to prevent, reached through this mode. A third session could then start the same work with no collision visible to either.
mutations.find: **If the brief names NO feature but a state file exists, CREATE the record and claim it.**
mutations.replace: If the brief names no feature, there is nothing to claim.

mutations.name: the-create-path-becomes-a-way-around-the-live-owner-check
mutations._mechanism: `owned_elsewhere` is the one branch that must never be softened by a more convenient entry point. A create path that skips the oracle takes a feature out from under a running session — exactly what `--force` exists to gate, reached without it.
mutations.find:
`start_fresh`, and `owned_elsewhere` **still stops** you; the create path is a way to own unclaimed
work, never a way around the live-owner check.
mutations.replace: `start_fresh`, so you may create and claim it.

mutations.name: the-feature-name-is-invented-rather-than-derived
mutations._mechanism: An invented name is unfindable by the sender and by the next reader: the brief asked for the work, and the claim must be traceable back to it. Two sessions inventing different names for one brief both believe they own it.
mutations.find:
brief's **slug** as the feature name — derived and traceable back to the document that asked for the
work, never invented:

mutations.name: a-positional-shell-arg-returns-to-the-skill-body
mutations._mechanism: A positional arg in a skill body is REWRITTEN by the slash-command renderer before the agent sees it. Measured twice on one line: it arrived as the literal word `read` and then `takeover`, matching the invocation, so the documented command printed the argument instead of the matching line. Silent, and wrong in a way the reader cannot see from the rendered text.
